plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with nodding, saucer-shaped white flowers that often take on a pink blush as they age. Its leathery, dark green leaves stay attractive through winter, and it thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family. Its flowers can push up through snow, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial bearing large, trumpet-shaped flowers on tall, sturdy stalks. Wild and cultivated forms bloom during the warm southern summer, and potted bulbs are forced to flower indoors in the Northern Hemisphere around the holidays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Native to tropical Americas and the Caribbean; cultivated worldwide, with flowering outdoors in South America, Australia and southern Africa at this time
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can bloom within 4 to 6 weeks of planting and may rebloom for decades with proper care. The flower stalks can grow several inches in a single day.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub or small tree with rose-like, layered blossoms. Early-season cultivars begin opening in late autumn and continue through winter, brightening gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (December to April in many regions)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, the Pacific Northwest and other mild-winter regions
plants.funFact: The tea plant, Camellia sinensis, is a close relative. In Japan, camellias have long been associated with samurai culture and are admired for their flowers falling intact.

plants.name: Nuytsia floribunda
plants.description: A remarkable tree that becomes covered in brilliant orange flower clusters at the height of the southern summer. In full bloom, the whole canopy appears to glow, and the display is among the most dramatic of Australia's native flora.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January)
plants.location: Southwestern Western Australia, in sandy soils and woodland areas
plants.funFact: It is the world's largest parasitic plant, tapping the roots of nearby plants for water and nutrients. Its roots can reportedly cut through buried cables when mistaking them for roots.
